items.title: Neem Baba's Origin
items.explanation: According to the text, Neem Baba was born millions of years ago somewhere in North India or Myanmar.

items.title: Names Given to Neem Baba
items.explanation: The name 'Neem' is given by Iranians. In Hindi, his name is Nimb, and he has other names like Nim, Leemba, Nimori, Nimbamond, Nimbe, and Nimo.

items.title: Uses of Neem for Farmers
items.explanation: If neem seed powder is mixed in water and sprayed on plants and trees, locusts do not eat them. It stops mosquito breeding and helps increase crop yield by saving crops from termites that eat roots.

items.title: Uses of Neem Leaves
items.explanation: Doctors advise using neem leaves for someone with measles because the neem leaves give comfort and do not allow germs to breed, which is useful when germs cause itching all over the body.

items.title: Uses of Neem Oil
items.explanation: Neem oil is used to make soaps and toothpaste.

items.title: Uses of Neem Wood
items.explanation: Furniture made from neem wood is not eaten by termites.

items.title: Uses of Neem Seeds
items.explanation: The powder of neem seeds can be mixed in water and sprayed on stagnant water around homes to stop mosquitoes from breeding, or it can be added to stored grains to protect them from insects.
